question.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$4{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}+18y=39?$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}+18y & =39 \\ 4{x}^{2}-3[{y}^{2}-6y] & =39 \\ 4{x}^{2}-3[(y-3)^{2}-9] & =39 \\ 4{x}^{2}-3(y-3)^{2}+27 & =39 \\ 4{x}^{2}-3(y-3)^{2} & =12 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the center is $(0,3).$
